body: Created folders belong to a game installation, not to one package, so they are not added to each package's `directories` (exclusive folders only). Keeping `list --json` as an array avoids breaking consumers. `--download` is opt-in because a dry run must have no network or cache side effect unless the user asks; it validates that the cache is outside every game before downloading and is rejected without `--dry-run` or for standalone archives.
summary: The milestone 4 live run found that `list` hid the created-directory ledger and that catalog dry runs could not plan files for uncached `https` archives. Modn now prints the per-game created folders in `modn list` text and reports them as `created_directories` in `doctor --json`. `list --json` stays an array of packages. `install --dry-run --download` fetches missing `https` archives into the verified cache; a dry run still never downloads by default and never writes the game.
title: Created-folder ledger is reported by list text and doctor JSON; dry runs download only with --download

body: Checkpoints: a red4ext 1.31.0 + cet 1.38.1; b redscript 0.5.32 + codeware 1.21.2; c virtual-atelier 1.6.4 with archivexl 1.28.6 and mod-settings 0.2.28; d equipment-ex 1.2.10 with tweakxl 1.12.0, then browser-extension 0.9.7, then no-intro-videos 0.8. Limits: the backup was a SHA-256 manifest only, so Steam verification is the only restore path. The c and d launch reports were general, with no specific in-game feature checks. Residue the user chose to keep: 21 runtime files, 7 folders, a rewritten redscript_rCURRENT.log, and 4 older redscript logs removed by redscript's rotation. The run's three Modn gaps were fixed in PRs #45 and #46. The raw manifests and diffs are outside the repository, in the user's local modn-live folder.
summary: On a real Steam Cyberpunk 2077 installation (game 3.0.88.46235), the 11-package prerequisite stack installed through `modn install` in four user-authorized checkpoints. The user launched the game after each checkpoint and reported success. `modn uninstall` removed all 11 packages (137 owned files) in reverse order. The game tree then matched the preflight manifest except for runtime files the game created.
title: Milestone 4 live Cyberpunk validation passed on 2026-11-02

body: Measured on 2026-11-02 with stable Rust on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: a default release build imports VCRUNTIME140.dll and eleven api-ms-win-crt-*-l1-1-0.dll files. A +crt-static build imports none of them. GitHub windows-latest runners have the Visual C++ Redistributable, so a runner smoke test alone cannot detect this dependency. The smoke test therefore searches the binary for C runtime DLL import names. Issue #47.
summary: The Release workflow builds modn.exe with RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=+crt-static, and the smoke test rejects any Visual C++ runtime DLL import.
title: Release modn.exe links the C runtime statically

body: Keeps: platform and dependency gotchas (NTFS case folding, 8.3 names, MoveFileEx, inode reuse, Windows verbatim paths, 7z solid blocks, ZipWriter duplicate names) and the clap help doc comments in apps/modn-cli/src/commands.rs, which are help text. crates/modn-core/src/lib.rs keeps #![warn(missing_docs)] and CI runs clippy with -D warnings, so public items need a doc or an expect. Claimed constraints that lost their comment: the 7z header bound (capabilities.rs, covered by tests/read_only_capabilities.rs) and the Lua proxy rawset caveat (runtime.rs, not enforced).
summary: All Rust, Lua, Python and TOML comments were removed except keeps. modn-core keeps doc comments on public items that state a contract. Docs that only restate an item name were replaced by #[expect(missing_docs, reason = ...)] on the parent struct, enum or impl.
title: Source comments removed; public docs required by missing_docs stay

body: Keeps: platform and dependency gotchas (NTFS case folding, 8.3 names, MoveFileEx, inode reuse, Windows verbatim paths, 7z solid blocks, ZipWriter and ZipArchive duplicate names) and the clap help doc comments in apps/modn-cli/src/commands.rs, which are help text. crates/modn-core/src/lib.rs keeps #![warn(missing_docs)] and CI runs clippy with -D warnings, so public items need a doc or an expect. Audit of 48 'never/must/only' claims from deleted comments: most already had tests. Four tests were added: host_answers_carry_no_host_path_or_handle (read_only_capabilities.rs), linked_state_root_cannot_redirect_registration_writes (buckets_cli.rs), unregistering_a_game_ends_its_directory_records (created_dirs_tests.rs), absent_or_replaced_owned_directory_refuses_uninstall_without_a_journal (generic_tests/directories.rs). Each was shown to fail when the guarded code was broken. Not encoded: the Lua proxy rawset caveat in runtime.rs (a non-guarantee; a test would freeze a weakness), 'registered paths are not canonicalized' in buckets.rs, and 'check conflicts before any download' in catalog_install.rs, which the current code does not do when --download is set.
